title: Count Every Possible Route (Backtracking)
real_world_story: A puzzle designer wants to know how many different solutions a small maze has. Every route from entrance to exit must be tried without revisiting any cell, so the difficulty can be tuned.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Small maze where 0 is a path and 1 is a wall
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Trying every direction and undoing each step to explore the next option

problem_statement: Given an R x C maze grid of 0 (free) and 1 (wall), a start cell (sr, sc) and a destination cell (dr, dc), count all valid routes from start to destination using 4-directional moves. A route may not step on walls, leave the grid, or visit any cell more than once.
task: Return the number of distinct valid routes from start to destination.
input_format: The first line contains two integers R and C. The next R lines each contain C integers (0 or 1). The final line contains four integers sr sc dr dc.
output_format: Print the number of distinct valid routes. Print 0 when no route exists.

examples.explanation: The two routes are right-then-down and down-then-right.

expected_algorithm.name: Backtracking
expected_algorithm.reason: Every simple path must be explored with visited marking and undo, which is exactly depth-first backtracking.

hint: Mark the current cell visited before recursing.
Unmark it after the recursive calls return.
real_world_takeaway: Backtracking enumerates every maze solution, which is how designers measure puzzle difficulty.
